open_with: Begin gently, on human terms first — acknowledge Frau Voss-Brenner's loss and thank her for making time. Then move naturally into the neutral, practical anchor point: the upcoming German inheritance tax instalment of EUR 3,400,000 due 1 October 2026. Frame this simply as "let's make sure this is comfortably taken care of" — a caretaking check-in, not a portfolio review. Let her set the pace; make clear explicitly that no changes will be made unless and until she wishes it.
do_not_lead_with: Do not lead with the portfolio findings — the 71.5% equity concentration relative to her conservative profile, or the single position exceeding mandate limits. She has explicitly asked for no changes for now, and raising these as "issues" would feel like pressure or a lecture at a moment when she needs steadiness, not education on mandate mechanics or risk exposure. Surfacing these unprompted risks undermining trust and could feel tone-deaf given her bereavement. Hold these in reserve only if she herself opens the door to reviewing holdings.
one_number: EUR 3,400,000 — the German inheritance tax instalment due 2026-10-01. This is the one figure to have ready and confirmed (funding source, timing, liquidity) so the conversation opens on reassurance and readiness, not on portfolio concerns.
